rules.h1sub: Drinking game rules & all card meanings
rules.setupLead: Two minutes and you’re ready to go.
rules.setup1: One standard deck of 52 cards, without Jokers.
rules.setup2: A big empty cup in the middle of the table – the King’s Cup.
rules.setup3: A drink for everyone – with or without alcohol, whatever each person likes.
rules.setup4: 3 to 12 players, sitting in a circle around the table.
rules.setupP: Shuffle the cards and spread them face down in a closed ring around the cup, so that every card touches its neighbours. The youngest player starts, then play goes clockwise.
rules.turnLead: On your turn you draw one card from the ring and do what it says.
rules.s1p: Take any card from the ring – carefully, without opening a gap.
rules.s2p: Turn it face up so everyone can see it.
rules.s3p: Every rank has its own rule (see The cards). Then it’s the next player’s turn.
rules.breakP: If you open a gap in the ring while drawing, you take a sip as a penalty. In many groups, whoever breaks the ring has to drink the King’s Cup straight away – agree on this beforehand.
rules.cardsH: The cards from Ace to King
rules.cardsLead: The rank decides what happens, the suit doesn’t matter. These are the most common rules:
rules.c_aP: Everyone starts drinking as soon as you start. Nobody may stop before the person to their right stops – you can stop whenever you like.
rules.c_2P: Pick someone: they take a sip.
rules.c_4P: Everyone touches the floor. The last one to do it takes a sip.
rules.c_7P: Everyone points to the ceiling. The last one takes a sip.
rules.c_8P: Choose a mate: whenever you drink, they drink too – until the next 8 is drawn.
rules.c_9P: Say a word. Going round the circle, everyone says a word that rhymes. Whoever hesitates or repeats one takes a sip.
rules.c_10P: Pick a category, e.g. beer brands or capital cities. Going round, everyone names something that fits. Whoever can’t think of anything takes a sip.
rules.c_jP: Make up a rule that applies until the end of the game, e.g. “no first names” or “only drink with your left hand”. Whoever breaks it takes a sip.
rules.c_qP: You are the Question Master until the next Queen. Whoever answers one of your questions takes a sip – unless they reply “Screw you, Question Master”.
rules.c_kP: Pour a little of your drink into the cup in the middle. What happens with the fourth King: see The Kings.
rules.cardsP: Many groups swap individual cards for their own rules – that’s part of the game. Good ideas are under Variants.
rules.kingsLead: The Kings decide when the game ends.
rules.kingsP: The fourth King: Whoever draws it has to drink the King’s Cup – in as many sips as they need. It doesn’t have to be in one go, and nobody has to finish a cup they don’t want to.
rules.endP: The game ends with the fourth King. If you want to keep playing, shuffle all the cards, rebuild the ring and start again with an empty cup.
rules.safeLead: King’s Cup should be fun for everyone – including the next morning.
rules.safe1: Only for adults of legal drinking age in your country.
rules.safe2: Always sips, never shots. Agree on small sips before you start.
rules.safe3: No one has to drink alcohol. Water, soft drinks and alcohol-free beer count just as much – including in the King’s Cup.
rules.safe4: Nothing gross in the cup. Only pour in drinks that go together, and never mix in anything that people don’t know about.
rules.safe5: Have water on the table, take breaks, and never drive after playing. If someone has had enough, they’re out – no discussion.
rules.varLead: King’s Cup is played differently at every table. Agree before the first card which of these rules you use:
rules.var1: Gender-neutral 5 and 6: 5 becomes Thumb Master (put your thumb on the table at any moment, the last one to copy you takes a sip), 6 becomes Never have I ever.
rules.var2: 4 = Social: Instead of touching the floor, everyone raises their glass and drinks together.
rules.var3: 7 = Buzz (Seven): Count around the circle; on every number containing a 7 or divisible by 7 (7, 14, 17, 21 …), you clap instead. Whoever gets it wrong drinks.
rules.var4: 8 = Snake Eyes: You become the Snake until the next 8: anyone who looks you in the eye takes a sip.
rules.var5: J = Never have I ever: Everyone holds up three fingers; whoever has done what you name lowers one and takes a sip.
rules.var6: Break the ring, drink the cup: Whoever opens a gap must drink the King’s Cup immediately, even before the fourth King.
rules.var7: Without alcohol: Instead of sips, players collect points or do small dares; the fourth King has to sing a song or tell an embarrassing story.
rules.faq1q: Is King’s Cup the same as Ring of Fire and Circle of Death?
rules.faq1a: Yes. It’s the same game with different names – depending on the country and group, also simply “Kings”. Only the rules for individual cards vary.
rules.faq2q: How many players do you need?
rules.faq2a: At least three, it gets really fun with five or more. With more than twelve, it takes a long time before it’s your turn again – then use two rings.
rules.faq3q: How long does a game last?
rules.faq3a: Usually 30 to 60 minutes, depending on the number of players and how quickly the Kings come up.
rules.faq4q: Do I have to drink the whole cup in one go?
rules.faq4a: No. Take as many sips as you need – and if you don’t want to finish it, you don’t have to. See Play responsibly.
rules.faq5q: How does the Waterfall work exactly?
rules.faq5a: Whoever draws the Ace starts drinking and everyone else starts at the same time. Going clockwise, you may only stop once the person before you (to your right) has stopped. So the last one in the circle drinks the longest – go with small sips.
rules.faq6q: What happens if the rule from the Jack contradicts another rule?
rules.faq6a: The newer rule wins. If the table can’t agree, a vote decides.
rules.faq7q: Can you play King’s Cup without alcohol?
rules.faq7a: Absolutely. With soft drinks, water or alcohol-free beer the game works just the same – or you use small dares instead of sips (see Variants).
rules.faq8q: Does the suit of the card matter?
rules.faq8a: No, only the rank counts. Some groups make red and black cards different, e.g. red 2 = give a sip, black 2 = take a sip.

info.similar: Ride the Bus, Beer Pong, Never Have I Ever
info.gearAlt: A deck of cards and a big cup
info.intro: King’s Cup is the classic for hostel common rooms and pre-drinks: no strategy, no score sheet, just a deck of cards and a rule for every card. Everyone knows a slightly different version – so agree on the rules before the first card.

strategy.sub: King’s Cup is mostly luck. But how you draw, how you handle the tricky cards and how you pace yourself decides whether you’re still having fun at the fourth King.
strategy.principle: You can’t choose which card you get – but you can choose how well you react. Quick reflexes, a good memory for the rules on the table and a sensible pace make the difference.
principleItems: Agree on the rules before the first card. Go through all thirteen cards and any variants up front, so nobody argues mid-game.
Stay alert when it’s not your turn. Floor, Heaven, the Waterfall and the Question Master catch anyone who is looking at their phone.
Keep track of what is in play. Every Jack adds a rule, every Queen gives the table a new Question Master and every 8 a new mate.
strategy.ringLead: The ring is the one thing you really control on your turn.
ringItems: Draw where the cards overlap least. A card that barely touches its neighbours comes out without moving them.
Slide, don’t lift. Hold the neighbouring card down with one finger and slide yours out sideways.
Take your time. There is no time limit – a careful draw is cheaper than a penalty sip.
Fix the ring together. If cards have been knocked out of place, push them back before the next draw, so nobody argues later about who opened the gap.
strategy.cardsLead: Most cards are over in a second. These ones reward a little planning.
strategy.c_a: If you draw it, you set the pace: stop after a short sip and the whole table can stop. Sitting at the end of the Waterfall? Take tiny sips – you’ll be drinking the longest.
strategy.c_8: Pick someone who drinks at a similar pace to you. Spread it around: always choosing the same person isn’t fun for long.
strategy.c_9: Start with a word that has lots of easy rhymes to keep the round going, or a rare one to end it quickly. Think of your rhyme while the others are still speaking.
strategy.c_10: Choose a category you know well and that has plenty of answers. Never pick one where you would run out first yourself.
strategy.c_j: The best rules are easy to remember and easy to break by accident, like “no pointing” or “say cheers before every sip”. Skip rules that leave someone out or make anyone uncomfortable.
strategy.c_q: Slip your questions into normal conversation – “Shall I get you some water?” works better than an obvious quiz. And when someone else is Question Master, keep “Screw you, Question Master” ready.
strategy.kingsLead: The cup in the middle grows with every King – what goes in decides how hard the fourth King is.
kingsItems: Pour in only a little. A small splash is enough. The fourth King should be a laugh, not a punishment – and it might be you.
Only drinks that go together. Never pour in anything that someone at the table can’t or won’t drink.
Count the Kings. After the third King, every draw is a gamble – that’s when the table gets loud.
The fourth King doesn’t have to finish the cup. As many sips as needed, and stopping is always allowed.
strategy.paceLead: The best players are the ones who are still at the table for the second round.
paceItems: Small sips, always. Almost every card can mean a sip – over an hour, that adds up.
Have water next to your drink and use it between turns.
Switch to alcohol-free whenever you like. Soft drinks count just as much for every rule.
Eat before you play. A round on an empty stomach ends early for everyone.
strategy.paceWarn: If someone has had enough, they’re out – no discussion. Never pressure anyone to drink, and never drive after playing.
mistakes: Starting without agreeing on the rules. Ten minutes of arguing about what the 7 means kills the mood.
Grabbing a card in a hurry. A rushed draw breaks the ring – and costs you a sip.
Forgetting your own rule. Nothing is funnier for the table than the person who made a rule breaking it.
Answering the Question Master. A quick “What?” is enough to get caught.
Filling the cup to the brim. Someone has to drink it at the fourth King – maybe you.
Taking big gulps. The game is long and the cards keep coming: sips, not gulps.

quick.rule: Draw one card from the ring around the cup, show it and follow its rule. Break the ring = take a sip. Play goes clockwise.
quick.c_a: everyone drinks; stop only after the person to your right
quick.c_2: pick someone to take a sip
quick.c_4: last to touch the floor sips
quick.c_k: pour a little of your drink into the cup
quick.kings1: 1st to 3rd King: pour a little into the cup
quick.kings4: 4th King: drink the cup – as many sips as you need. Game over.
safe: Sips, never shots – and no one has to drink alcohol.
Water on the table, breaks allowed, never drive afterwards.
Had enough? Then you’re out – no discussion.
